simple.meaning: אַשְׁפָּה (ʼashpâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a quiver or arrow-case.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Job 39:23. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַשְׁפָּה (H827) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אַשְׁפָּה (ʼashpâh) / H827 is traced through Job 39:23, Psalms 127:5, Isaiah 22:6, Isaiah 49:2 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H827. ashpah אַשְׁמָּה noun feminine quiver for arrows (Assyrian išpatu Dl K 29 ) ׳א literal as part of warlike equipment Job 39:23 ; Isa 22:6 ; figurative in simile of sons of one's youth as arrows (weapons which the father may wield) Psa 127:5 מֵהֶם אֶתאַֿשְׁמָּתוֺ מִלֵּא אֲשֶׁר הַגֶּבֶר אַשְׁרֵי the happiness of the man that hath filled his quiver with them ! of Yahweh's quiver, in metaphor of prophet as arrow of ׳י Isa 49:2 הִסְתִּירָ֑נִי בְּאַשְׁמָּתוֺ בָּרוּר לְחַץ וַיְשִׂימֵנִי and he made me into a polished arrow, in his quiver he hid me ; also of quiver in which ׳י has his arrows of chastisement, אַשְׁמָּתוֺ בְּנֵי , i.e. his arrows Lam 3:13 (|| חֵץ 3:12 ). אַשְׁמּה quiver , see under the word
definitions.rootNote: perhaps (feminine) from the same as 825 (in the sense of covering );

occurrences.englishText: Happy is the man who has his quiver full of them.
Elam carried his quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen; and Kir uncovered the shield.
He has made my mouth like a sharp sword.
Their quiver is an open tomb. They are all mighty men.
He has caused the shafts of his quiver to enter into my kidneys.
